text: The selected section changes the list and its filters. Badges count the activity in each section, so you can see where items are waiting.
Shows your rating activity. The rating group separates sent, received and mutual interest; its count belongs to the selected group.
Switches to conversations and their context filters. Rating groups stay separate from chat activity.
Switches to event activity, with event-specific categories and date views. It does not change a rating or join an event.
Selects whose interest you are reviewing: yours, other people’s or mutual ratings. The badge counts profiles in that group.
Includes community suggestions alongside individual ratings. This changes the source of the recommendations you review.
Profiles you have rated appear here. This records your outgoing interest; it does not mean the other person has rated you back.
People who rated you appear here. Their interest is incoming; you can inspect their profiles before deciding how to respond.
View people you have rated who have also rated you. The badge shows the number of mutual ratings.
Keeps profiles of people marked as met together, so you can return to those connections after discovery.
Shows pair suggestions you sent to other people. This tracks your recommendations separately from your own individual interest.
Shows pair suggestions other people sent you. A recommendation is their suggestion, not an automatic mutual match.
Sorting changes which cards appear first while retaining the selected rating group. Choose time or relevance to suit what you want to review.
Places recent activity first, so newer interactions are easier to find. It changes order, not the recorded ratings.
Prioritizes relevance instead of time, helping you review stronger matches earlier. Your saved ratings remain unchanged.
Focuses on earlier activity when you want to revisit it. The selected rating group still determines which profiles belong in the list.
Grouping changes how the list is divided into days, weeks, months or distance ranges. It does not change ratings or group membership.
Groups activity into months for a wider time overview. Calendar arrows move the period while your filters remain active.
Group cards by week to compare activity over time. Use the calendar arrows to move between weeks.
Groups activity by day, making a particular date easier to revisit. Your selected rating group and sorting still apply.
Groups profiles by distance so nearby people are easier to compare. Distance changes the grouping, not the interest already recorded.
Gives the cards more screen space for comparison. Leaving fullscreen returns to the same rating list and filters.
The star summarizes this card’s rating. Its details show the associated rating information and available actions.
Move to the previous cards or calendar period in the selected view. Your group and sorting stay active.
Move to the next cards or calendar period in the selected view. Your group and sorting stay active.
Dragging changes how much space each person’s card gets. It only adjusts the comparison layout; neither profile nor rating changes.
Opens the profile related to this card, so you can inspect the person connected to the activity. This is useful when an activity card refers to a person other than its main profile.
The photo is divided into one clickable section per image: three photos give thirds, four give quarters. Tap a section to select that photo without opening a popup.
The eye opens this person’s profile, while the activity list remains behind the profile popup. Close the profile popup to return to the same activity card.
Move the slider from 1 to 10 to change your rating for the visible person or pair. Use Save to record it. A read-only rating cannot be adjusted.
Press this button to save the selected value for the current card. Moving the slider only prepares the value; Save confirms your change.
This badge opens the person connected to the activity card. It gives you the context behind the rating before you continue with the list.
This badge opens the people or members related to the activity. Use it to review who is involved without losing your place in the rating list.
Actions belong to this activity card and depend on your access. The guide opens the menu to explain them without executing an action.
Closes the Activities popup and returns to the screen behind it; it dismisses this view only. Your place in the underlying screen remains where it was.
Use these shortcuts to choose profile preferences, filter suggestions, or open your rating history.
These cards show people in your current discovery view. Badges summarize activity, while the card controls open photos, profiles, and rating actions.
Choose how people are matched before you review cards. Changing this mode changes the suggestions and available search fields.
Browse one profile at a time and compare it with your preferences. Use this when you want to decide separately for each person.
Find suggestions connected through mutual friends. The extra search fields help narrow the list to people in the same social circle.
Browse people connected to your existing network. This view helps you discover profiles through relationships you already share.
Explore profiles beyond your current connections. Use this view when you want to broaden the people you can discover.
Set interests and profile criteria to focus the suggestions you see. The filter badge shows when criteria are active, so you can tell why the list is narrower.
The Ratings shortcut on Home opens your rating activity. From there, the rating group menu lets you review likes you sent, received, matched, or marked as met.
Move the slider from 1 to 10 to express how strongly this profile fits you. The chosen value is saved when you press Go.
The photo is divided into one clickable section per image: three photos give thirds, four give quarters. Tap a section to select that photo without opening a popup.
Use the eye button to see the person’s profile, experience, and other details. Your current discovery list stays available behind the profile popup.
Go is a button: it saves the selected affinity value and advances to the next suggested profile. Adjust the slider before pressing it.
Switch between ratings, conversations, and events. The badges show matching items, and choosing a section changes the list below.
Filter conversations by their context, such as events, groups, or support. This narrows the list so you can find the relevant chat faster.
Each row opens a conversation or its available actions. The list follows your selected context, so changing the filter above changes which chats appear.
Choose a conversation to open its messages and continue where you left off. The surrounding filters determine which conversations are included here.
Enter your message here and send it to the open conversation. Replies, shared items, and any selected context stay attached to this chat.
Send the text you have written to the current conversation. Check the recipient and context first, since sending makes the message visible to its participants.
Open a message menu to reply, react, or use other available actions. These controls apply to one message, keeping the rest of the conversation unchanged.
Open the plus menu to attach a photo, voice clip, poll, event, or asset. This lets you share context in the conversation instead of sending text alone.
Close this popup when you are done here. The guide ends with this screen, while the parent view stays open if the app keeps it underneath.
The pencil opens your photo slots for upload, replacement and removal. Closing that popup returns to the draft; Save profile persists the changes.
Export your event schedule for use in another calendar. The export copies calendar data; it does not change event participation.
Affiliate contains your referral link, API keys and AI-client connections through MCP. Admin accounts open their management API settings here.
Review your name and core profile details so people can recognize you. Accurate information makes your profile and event introductions clearer.
Write a short introduction. This text helps people understand who you are before meeting you.
Your birth date determines your age and horoscope. Check it before saving your profile.
Choose the gender shown on your profile and used in discovery.
Choose your city so discovery and events can use the right location.
Enter your height in centimetres. It can be used in profile filters.
Choose the description that fits you. This value is part of your profile and discovery preferences.
Describe your work. Use the visibility control beside the field to choose who can see it.
Open your workplace history to add or review experience. Changes are saved with your profile.
Open your education history to add or review schools. The visibility control sets who can see this information.
Select the languages you speak. They appear in your profile and can be used when filtering people.
Choose interests that describe what you enjoy. Their visibility setting controls who can see them.
Select the option that describes your drinking habits. Use the adjacent control to set its visibility.
Select your smoking habits and choose who can see them with the adjacent visibility control.
Choose how often you exercise. The adjacent visibility control determines who can see your answer.
Choose the pets that are part of your life. You can set this field’s visibility separately.
Choose the option that reflects your plans. Decide who can see it with the visibility control.
Choose the answer that fits your situation. The visibility control lets you keep this detail private.
Choose how you prefer a connection to develop. Its visibility is controlled separately.
Select the way you prefer to communicate. Set who can see it with the adjacent visibility control.
Choose the answer you want to include in your profile. You control who can see this detail.
Choose the option that describes your beliefs, and set its visibility separately.
Select the values that matter to you. Use the visibility control to choose who can see them.
Choose who can see this profile. Visibility affects discovery and profile access, while saved profile details remain unchanged.
Save your edits when the sections are ready. The updated information is then used by your profile view and the surfaces where others discover you.
The large preview shows the selected photo. Selecting another filled slot changes this preview; selecting it again opens replacement.
Choose a file from your device for this empty slot. Wait for upload to finish; uploading a file does not save the whole profile or publish a feed post.
A filled slot first selects its photo. Click the selected slot again to choose a replacement; check the new preview before saving the parent editor.
Copies the image link to the clipboard. It does not duplicate the photo into another slot or save your profile.
Removes this photo from the edited collection. Review the remaining images before saving the parent profile, event, asset or post.
The dots move between pages of photo slots. This only changes which slots are visible; it does not reorder or remove images.
Opens the photo’s caption and location or event link. A red pencil means its required event is missing: link an event before saving the feed post.
This location belongs to the photo. Keep it within 240 characters; longer text blocks saving its details.
Describe what the photo shows in up to 40 characters. The remaining count is a character limit, not a required minimum.
Applies these details to the current image draft. A required event must be selected and the location must fit the limit; save the parent editor separately.
Browse the available photos. If there is more than one page, use the arrows or page dots. This view does not change the images.
The card brings together the person’s photos and basic introduction. Use its photo controls to browse images before reading the detailed information below.
This section shows profile details and any visibility badges attached to them. Those indicators help explain why some information may be visible only to certain people.
Review the person’s experience entries to learn more about their background. Each entry adds context to the profile without changing its basic details.
Move through the available photos to see more of the person’s profile. The selected photo changes the image in this view, not the person’s saved profile.
Read the profile introduction and personal notes to understand what matters to them. These details add context beyond the short card preview.
Information is grouped by topic, and only details shared with you are shown. Use these sections for context without assuming anything that is hidden.
The dots move between pages of photo slots. This only changes which slots are visible; it does not reorder or remove images.
Enter a name to narrow the contacts list. This is useful when you have saved many people and want to open one profile or contact method quickly.
Choose a group to show a specific set of contacts. Switching groups changes the list, while the search term can further narrow the visible people.
Contact cards provide shortcuts to profiles, conversations, and saved contact methods. Their badges and actions depend on the person and the details available.
Save a person as a contact to make future conversations and profile access easier. Contact status is managed separately from ratings and event participation.
Open the contact’s profile from the card to review shared details. This is useful when you need to confirm who a saved contact is.
Open the contact menu to see available actions such as editing or removing the shortcut. These actions manage your saved relationship, not the person’s profile.
Browse the saved people and open the one you need. Search and group filters help you find a contact without changing their stored details.
Show the previous page or calendar period. Your current filters remain active.
Show the next page or calendar period. Your current filters remain active.
Add a clear photo so people can recognize the item before requesting it. A representative image reduces confusion when several assets are available.
Choose a short name that identifies the item in lists and requests. A specific title helps members distinguish it from similar equipment.
Choose the category that best describes this item. Categorization places it in the right asset list and makes it easier to find.
This form defines the item other people can request. Add accurate details so members can compare it and understand what they will receive.
The form groups the item’s identity, availability and terms into sections. Complete the relevant parts so requests use the right details and limits.
Use this line for the detail people need at a glance, such as size or intended use. It appears beside the title in compact asset cards.
Set how many units can be requested at once. This limit helps prevent more people from reserving the asset than you can provide.
Enter the number of units needed for this assignment. The available range follows the event’s capacity so the request stays within its limits.
Add a product or reference page when people need more specifications. The link gives them context without crowding the asset description.
Explain the item’s condition, contents and any practical limits. Clear details help someone decide whether it fits their needs before sending a request.
Set where the asset is located so borrowers know where pickup or use will happen. A precise place makes coordination easier during the event.
Set the route used for this event assignment. This is useful when a transport asset follows a route that differs from its usual listing.
Review the price and any time-based charges before publishing the asset. These values are used to show the cost during a request or checkout.
Add terms borrowers must read or approve before completing a request. Clear rules protect both sides and explain how the item should be used or returned.
Choose who can discover or request this asset. The setting controls whether it appears broadly or only to a narrower event audience.
Save the details and make the asset available according to its visibility. Check the required fields first so the listing can be used immediately.
Save the route for this event assignment. The updated path is then used to coordinate transport with the event participants.
These rows explain the base amount and applied adjustments. Review the total after discounts, quantity and timing rules, not the base amount alone.
This is the calculated total in the displayed currency. A preview is not a completed payment; the final action determines what is submitted.
The short summary may omit details. Open the policies to read their full text before accepting or submitting the request.
Required terms apply to the request. Optional terms have a separate approval choice; the badge distinguishes these two cases.
This checkbox controls approval of this optional policy only. It does not submit the request or accept other optional policies.
This is the starting price before enabled pricing rules adjust it. Review the preview to see the amount produced by the full configuration.
All configured price amounts use this currency. Changing it changes the denomination of the entered amounts; check every price before applying.
Sets how tax is represented in this pricing configuration. Check the selected option and the resulting price summary before applying it.
The charge type determines whether the amount applies per person or to the configured resource or booking. It changes how the base price is multiplied or shared.
Limits how low the calculated price can fall after adjustments. Use the preview to check how this floor interacts with discounts.
Limits the calculated price after adjustments. Check the preview so demand or timing rules cannot produce an unintended amount.
Applies the selected rounding to the calculated price. Compare the final preview amount before saving the configuration.
Applies these pricing settings to the parent editor. Save the asset or event there to persist the complete change.

This toggle filters the list to assets with requests that still need attention. Its badge shows the pending count, and switching it off restores all assets.
Each card summarizes a vehicle and its availability. Open a card to review details or use its actions to manage requests and event assignments.
Open the owner profile to see who is responsible for this item. That context can help you decide whether to request or assign it.
Review availability, requests, or quantity from this badge. Its count helps you see whether the item fits your current plan.
Open the card menu to edit, assign, or manage requests for this item. Only actions available for its type and your role are shown.
Open the editor for this asset’s details, capacity, pricing and policies. Save to apply changes.
Open the asset details to review its availability and requirements.
Open the request form to review dates, quantity and any payment before confirming.
Review this asset’s availability and reservations for the selected period.
Review the asset’s capacity and current assignments before changing allocation.
Open the transport route and its stops to review pickup and destination details.
Open a conversation with the owner about this item. No message is sent automatically.
Open sharing options for this asset so others can view its details.
Open a report about the owner. Describe the issue before submitting it.
Make this item available to its configured audience. Check its details and visibility first.
Withdraw this item from its published audience. Review the confirmation before continuing.
Start removing this item. Read the confirmation before completing a destructive action.
Changes to this asset are saved in its editor. Availability, price and policies affect later requests, so review them before saving.
This badge counts pending requests attached to the card. It is separate from accepted participation or occupied capacity; a pending request is not a confirmed place.
The label distinguishes waiting, blocked or inactive items from confirmed ones. Waiting for approval requires a decision before participation is accepted.
The reference link opens outside the app. It can provide specifications that supplement the asset listing; it does not reserve the item.
Starts taking over this asset when your current access allows it. Check the confirmation: this changes responsibility for the item.

Choose which events to show, such as invitations, drafts, or active events. Counts on the options help you see where attention is needed.
Choose upcoming or past activity. This changes which events appear without modifying any event.
Choose Day, Week, Month or Distance where available. Calendar views use period arrows; lists use scrolling.
Open event discovery to find activities outside your current list. Discovery has its own filters and guide.
Open the available creation and management shortcuts. The guide explains them without performing an action.
Browse event cards and open an event to see its details. The selected category above controls the cards shown here and helps you focus on what matters.
Open the host profile from the event card to check who is organizing it. This can help you decide whether the event and its community are relevant to you.
Open the member list from this badge to review attendees and available participation details. Any pending count signals requests that still need attention.
Open the event’s action menu to view the actions available for this event and your role. Use it to continue with management, sharing, or participation tasks.
Open the event workspace to manage its details, stages and participants.
Open the event details and available stages. This does not join the event.
Open the editor to change event details. Changes take effect only when you save.
Open a message to the event’s participants. Review the audience and text before sending.
Open the sharing options for this event so you can send its link to others.
Open the external information link supplied for this event. It may lead to another website.
Start cancelling this event. Review the effect on participants and payments before confirming.
Start deleting this event. Read the confirmation carefully before removing it.
Follow this organizer to find their eligible events in Followed. It does not join an event.
Stop following this organizer. Your existing event participation is separate from following.
Start a request to participate. Review any requirements, options and price before confirming.
Open booking to review attendance options and payment. Nothing is confirmed by opening it.
Request a place on the waiting list. This is not a confirmed place at the event.
Start leaving this event. Review the participation and refund details before confirming.
Keep this event in your watchlist so you can return to it later. This does not join the event.
Remove this event from your watchlist. Your event participation stays separate.
Open a conversation with the organizer about this event. You can review the message before sending.
Open the reporting form for the organizer. Explain the issue before submitting it for review.
Show the previous week or month in the calendar. The selected event group and filters stay active.
Show the next week or month in the calendar. The selected event group and filters stay active.

Shows the saved booking and its payment state. Opening the summary does not charge again or create another booking.
Restores the existing checkout so you can review options and payment. Nothing is finalized merely by reopening it.
Returns to the pending booking and shows what remains to complete. Check its current payment state before submitting again.
Shows the event you were invited to and the available response. Reviewing it does not accept the invitation.
Starts accepting this invitation. Review any participation options or payment shown before completing the flow.
Declines this invitation instead of accepting a place. Check the event and confirmation before proceeding.
Starts the cancellation and refund flow for this booking. The confirmation shows the applicable refund before you commit.
Returns a removed item through the available restore flow. Review the confirmation and resulting state before applying it.
Visibility limits the audience: public, friends or invitees. It is separate from approval, which controls whether a join request is accepted.
Add photos that show what the event is about. They appear on event cards and help invitees recognize the event before opening its details.
Choose a name that tells invitees which event this is. It appears on cards and in related views, making the event easier to find and distinguish.
This is the event’s minimum attendance setting. Once published, the minimum is locked; the maximum can still be adjusted within the allowed limits.
This is the event’s participant limit. Raising it makes room for more participants; existing participation can restrict how far you lower it.
Add a place so participants know where the event happens. A precise location also helps people plan travel and check distance.
Blind Event hides attendees from each other before the event. Turn it off when guests should be able to preview who is coming.
Choose up to five topics. People can find the event through topic filters; accurate topics help it reach the right audience.
When enabled, invitations use mutual preferences to find suitable people. When off, you control invitations manually.
Accepted attendees receive a QR ticket. An event manager can check it in once; this switch controls entry tickets, not the event price.
Auto approve off: join requests wait for an event admin. On: confirmed bookings can proceed without that manual approval.
Explain what participants will do and what they should know beforehand. Helpful details set expectations and make it easier to decide whether to join.
This link gives guests an external information page. Use it for details that belong outside the event description.
Enable sub-events when the programme needs separate activities or stages. Each definition adds its own timing and participation rules.
The mode determines how stages work: a programme, a scored competition, or rotating conversations. Choose it before defining the stages.
Use Standard for activities without tournament progression or rotating tables. Sub-events can be mandatory or optional parts of the programme.
Tournament stages organize groups, scores and progression. Their configuration determines how participants move through the competition.
Mingle assigns people to tables across timed rounds. Group size, round length and breaks determine how many conversations fit the event.
This view shows the existing event mode. It cannot be changed here; the available stages follow that mode.
Timeline makes the running order easy to compare. Cards show individual stage details. Switching views does not change the programme.
For Standard and Tournament, this opens a new stage draft. For Mingle, it opens table size and round timing settings.
Configure optional stages or tournament groups for this event. A clear structure helps participants understand the schedule and where each activity belongs.
Choose when the event starts and ends. The date and time determine how it appears in schedules and help guests avoid conflicts.
Define the time slots people can choose. Separate slots make capacity and attendance easier to manage when the event has several sessions.
Set the cost and payment terms participants will see. Clear pricing helps people understand the commitment before confirming a place.
Add rules participants may need to read or accept. Clear policies explain expectations and can appear in the checkout or request flow.
Saving applies this draft to the event. Review capacity, timing and participation settings first; these affect the guests’ options.

Each card describes one activity or round. Its order, duration and offset determine how it fits into the event.
This badge shows the planned duration. It helps you check whether all stages fit inside the event dates.
Shows whether an activity is mandatory or optional. In Tournament and Mingle mode it identifies the stage or round instead.
Edit opens this stage’s timing and participation rules. Delete removes its definition from the draft; review the schedule afterward.
Opens a separate editor for this stage. Its timing, capacity and tournament rules belong to this stage, not the whole event.
Removes this stage from the event draft. Check the remaining sequence and timing before saving the event.
Mandatory activities belong to the main event. Optional activities can have their own places and price. Tournament stages stay mandatory.
Applies this stage to the event draft. Required fields must be valid; the event itself is persisted with its own Save action.
Participants use this name to distinguish activities or rounds. A name is required before this stage can be applied.
Sets the attendance range of this optional activity. Its capacity can differ from the main event’s capacity.
Places this stage before, during or after the reference activity. The anchor and offset determine its relative timing.
Choose the existing stage used for relative positioning. Together with placement and offset it anchors the new activity in time.
Adds a time offset in minutes to the relative schedule. Use it to leave room for a break or movement between activities.
Describe the activity or round and any preparation it needs. This required text helps guests decide what they are joining.
Reserves this many minutes for the stage. Changing it affects how the stage fits with the rest of the schedule.
Sets the time window for this activity. Check it against the parent event’s dates and any other stages.
This activity can have a more specific meeting point than the main event. Give participants enough detail to find it.
Optional activities may have a separate price. Guests review the selected activities and their costs during checkout.
Mandatory activities do not have a separate activity price. Their cost belongs to the main event’s pricing.
Sets the lower size bound for tournament groups in this stage. Check it together with the maximum and available participants.

Close this view to return to the event. Your saved groups and results remain attached to the selected event stage.

When score entry is available, managers can record a score or match result. Results affect standings and advancement; verify the participants and values.
Opens this group’s editable configuration. Changes belong to this group; review its capacity and identity before saving.
Starts removal of this group. Inspect its participants and current stage before confirming a deletion.
Opens this group’s member list. Accepted and pending counts differ; pending requests still require the applicable approval.
Opens transport assigned to this group. Review available places and requests in that resource list.

Choose how many people meet at each table in a round. Smaller tables create more direct conversations; larger ones fit bigger events.
Set how many conversation rounds the event should run. More rounds let participants meet more people but make the activity longer.
Choose how many minutes participants have at each table. Leave enough time for a useful conversation while keeping the event on schedule.
Set a short pause for moving to the next table. A break helps participants change seats without cutting into conversation time.
Ask the assignment logic to balance groups using the event’s available gender information. This can shape table composition when participants have shared those details.
Apply these settings to the event’s mingle rounds. The organizer can then start tables using the chosen group size and timing.
Close this panel and return to the event editor. Use Save if you want the changed round settings to take effect.
Review the selected item, quantity and dates before continuing. The summary helps catch a mismatch before you submit a request or payment.
Choose or confirm the payment method and review its status. The payment step completes the request only after the required details are accepted.
Borrowing uses the chosen period to calculate availability and price. Joining an event assignment uses that activity’s fixed start and end.
Review the refund terms that apply to this request. They explain what may be returned if plans change after payment.
The button states the next action: send a request, continue to payment or finalize. A pending request is not yet an approved place.
Close the checkout flow and return to the asset screen. If you have not confirmed the request, it will not be submitted by closing.
This identifies the asset you are about to use. Check its name and photo before requesting a place; the activity may offer several similar items.
Capacity describes what the asset can accommodate. It is not the number of places you personally request or a guarantee that every place is free.
This quantity belongs to the asset or assignment shown here. Locked values are information; joining an assigned vehicle or stay requests one place.
Check the condition, included equipment and practical limits. The request refers to this described asset, so resolve unclear details with the owner first.
Borrowing follows quantity and duration rules. For an assigned resource, per-member pricing charges each person; shared pricing divides the total between participants.
Required lending terms always apply. Optional approvals can be selected separately; read the terms before submitting your request.
The location identifies the accommodation or pickup point. It belongs to the listed asset; it does not change when you open checkout.
These rows explain the base amount and applied adjustments. Review the total after discounts, quantity and timing rules, not the base amount alone.
This is the calculated total in the displayed currency. A preview is not a completed payment; the final action determines what is submitted.
The short summary may omit details. Open the policies to read their full text before accepting or submitting the request.
Required terms apply to the request. Optional terms have a separate approval choice; the badge distinguishes these two cases.
This checkbox controls approval of this optional policy only. It does not submit the request or accept other optional policies.
This is the payment state. A pending or failed payment is not paid; participation may also require separate organizer approval.
Select the method for this checkout and check its displayed card details. Selecting a card alone does not authorize the payment.
People who register through your link are attributed to you. The badge counts those registrations; it does not grant access to their accounts.
Your client sends API requests to this address. Use this installation’s exact URL; the client key determines which account it acts for.
Each key connects a client to the issuing profile or group. Keep separate keys so one client’s access can be revoked independently.
A new key allows a supported client to connect. Its secret appears once: copy it into that client’s settings, never into a public message.
Connected means this key has been claimed by a client. Expiry ends its validity; the prefix identifies the key without revealing its secret.
Revoking invalidates this key. That client loses API access with it; the other keys remain independently managed.
MCP lets an AI client read help. With approved access, it can also use permitted event, encounter, creation and invitation actions.
Paste this MCP URL into your AI client and choose Connect. Sign in and check the displayed profile and group before approving access.
These are URL-based connections you approved. Each acts within the displayed account’s permissions; access does not bypass ownership rules.
Check the client name, last use and expiry to recognize active access. An expired permission must be renewed before the client can use it again.
Details identify the client and callback address. Revoke ends this connection’s access after confirmation.
Use Advanced only for a client that needs an ID and secret. Normal URL-based Connect does not need a manually generated key.
These keys belong to manually configured MCP clients. URL-based OAuth permissions are managed separately on the previous screen.
Generation creates a client ID and a one-time secret. Copy both into the intended client’s settings; do not paste the secret into chat.
Open the help panel for connection guidance. It explains what information a client needs and where to configure it.
Close these settings and return to the previous screen. Existing client keys keep their current access until you revoke them.
Revenue summarizes paid purchases attributed to your referrals, including refunds. These amounts are not your earned commission.
Counts paid purchases attributed to people you invited. It is a purchase count, so it need not equal the number of invited users.
Counts attributed paid event bookings. This separates event booking activity from the overall purchase count.
The total attributed purchase amount before refunds. The selected display currency converts the summary; it does not change any payment.
Refunds reduce the attributed purchase total. Compare them with the original total to understand the amount remaining after refunds.
This is attributed purchase revenue minus refunds. It is not a payout balance or earned affiliate commission.
The affiliate commission rate and eligibility rules are not set. This summary measures referral revenue, not money currently owed to you.
Choose the member who handed over the money. Linking the receipt to the right person keeps the payment history accurate.
Enter the amount you actually received. This value is added to the payment history totals in the selected currency.
Use the currency that was handed over. The saved history entry and any later refund calculation use this amount and currency together.
Add a short reference such as what the payment covers. The note stays with this history entry so it is easier to recognize later.
Save after checking the payer, amount, and currency. The cash receipt then appears in payment history and updates the related totals.
Close this form without saving the receipt. You return to payment history, where you can open the form again if needed.
The pencil opens the active profile: photos, personal details and preferences. Save in that editor to apply changes.
Switch between your personal profile and available group workspaces. The selected workspace determines whose content and permissions you use.
Opens notifications for the current account. The badge counts unread updates; muted notifications and a missing location can affect availability.
Turns the explanation launcher on or off across the app. Each guide includes only steps available on the current screen.
Opens help, privacy, terms and account actions. Read the relevant confirmation before choosing a destructive action such as deleting the account.
Browse shared photos or create a post. Each uploaded feed photo needs an event link before the post can be submitted for moderation.
Shows events from followed organizers. Following helps you find their events; it does not book a place or join those events.
Review your groups, invitations and requests, or explore other communities. Membership and acting in a group workspace are separate choices.
Shows feedback-based impressions of you as host and attendee. These describe past experiences, rather than editable profile preferences.
Review pending and completed event feedback. This is feedback about participation; application support is available separately in Settings.
Shows your rating activity and its available filters. Rating a profile is separate from accepting an invitation or joining an event.
Opens conversations for events, groups, contacts and support. Use context filters to find the correct conversation before sending a message.
Review invitations and their event details before responding. An invitation alone does not mean your participation or payment is confirmed.
Find events you attend or manage, plus pending and other states. The scope selector separates these roles and lifecycle states.
Review payment records and refund states. A pending refund is still in progress; opening this list does not start a payment or refund.
Manage transport assets and inspect their availability. Owning a vehicle and joining a place on an event’s assigned vehicle are different actions.
Manage accommodation assets, capacity and availability. Booking or joining an assigned stay has its own review and confirmation flow.
Manage supply assets and quantities. Event assignments and contributions determine how those supplies are used by a particular activity.
View available ticket records and their state. Tickets represent entry rights; payment history records the associated financial transactions.
Review contacts and incoming requests. The badge highlights pending requests, so it can differ from the total number of saved contacts.
Closes the avatar menu without opening another section.
Opens application installation and permission settings. Device permissions control which features can use notifications or location.
Opens sharing options for this application. It shares the application link rather than your private profile settings.
Opens the active help document. Its version badge identifies the published help revision available in this installation.
Opens application feedback for questions or suggestions. Use event feedback separately to describe an attended event.
Opens the project’s issue page in another tab. Describe what you did, what happened and what you expected.
Opens the current privacy document. Its version identifies which published data-handling terms you are reading.
Opens the current application terms. These describe application use; individual events and assets may have additional policies.
Opens the account deletion flow. Read its consequences before confirming; closing the guide does not delete the account.
Signs you out of the current session. You must sign in again to continue actions that require your account.
Review people and roles for the group, asset or conversation named above. Membership state determines who can participate and which requests need a decision.
Turn this filter on to focus on people whose requests are not resolved yet. Turn it off to return to the full member list.
Opens invitations for this group, asset or conversation. Review recipients before sending; opening the chooser does not send invitations.
Returns to the screen that opened this member list. Closing the guide alone keeps the member list open.
The menu applies to this person’s membership. Role and participation state determine which actions are available.
Shows the person’s participation across activities. Use it to understand their assignments before changing membership.
Organizer only separates management from attendance. Count as participant includes this organizer in event participation.
Gives this member management permissions in the current group, asset or conversation. Review the scope before changing their role.
Revocation removes this member’s manager role. Review the confirmation to distinguish role changes from removing participation.
Stepping down removes your management role in this context. It does not promote someone else in your place.
Accepts a pending membership request in this context. Check the person and the group or asset named above before confirming.

Ends your membership in the current context. Review the confirmation for its effect on your access and any linked bookings.

A report sends the described concern for review. It does not directly change the reported person’s role or participation.
Invitation pending: the guest must respond. Waiting for approval: an admin must decide. Waiting for payment: payment is unfinished. The icon also distinguishes member roles.
This label flags payment still due or a removed membership. The menu shows which actions are available in the current state.
Opens the profile details this person makes visible to you. Viewing a profile does not change their membership or role.
Switch between upcoming and earlier availability records. An empty current list can still have completed bookings under Earlier.
Choose how bookings are arranged in time. Calendar views help compare occupied periods; the list shows individual requests and assignments.
All combines the activity types. Use the filter to focus on pending requests, borrowed items or event assignments before taking action.
Filters records inside the selected date range. Changing the filter only changes the list; it does not accept or cancel a request.
Sets which dates this list covers. Review overlapping usage here before accepting another request for the asset.
Shows bookings, requests and assignments for this asset. Dates, quantity and state explain how each record affects availability.
Review who uses the asset, for which activity and during which dates. Its menu acts on this record, not every use of the asset.
Pending still needs a decision. Borrowed means an accepted request; Assigned identifies an event assignment. The number is the reserved quantity.
Available actions depend on your role and this record’s state. Management, approval and removal have different effects.
Opens the management screen for this assignment. Inspect members, resource details and available actions there.
Accepts this pending asset request. Check its dates, quantity and availability before confirming.
Removes the selected request or assignment. Review the confirmation for any booking or payment consequences.
Gives the person management rights for this assignment. Review who receives the role before confirming.
Removes the person’s manager role for this assignment. This is separate from removing the request itself.
Closes this availability view. No request is accepted or removed by closing it.
Changes the order of the results without changing availability or sending a request. Choose the order that helps you compare suitable assets.
Filters vehicles, accommodation or supplies. Availability is evaluated for the selected type and dates.
These dates determine availability and pricing. Changing them can change which assets you can request.
Compare the owner, capacity, price and availability for the chosen dates. Opening a card does not reserve the asset.
Opens the owner’s visible profile. It helps identify the provider before you request their asset.
Opens the borrow review when this asset is available. Check dates, quantity, price and policies before confirming a request.
An unavailable badge cannot open borrowing. Review the date range or another asset; availability can differ between periods.
Keeps requests you started reviewing. Open one to continue; a saved draft alone is not a confirmed reservation.
